name: Nullvault Cleanroom Iso-Suit Type-C
description:
Crisp white single-piece coverall with sealed hood, integrated booties, and triple-layer glove cuffs. Shell is electrostatically dissipative polyethylene composite — stiff, crinkles audibly when moved, and carries a faint antiseptic smell that never fully washes out. Designed for Class-10 cleanroom chip fabrication environments and geneware clinic sterile theaters.

Face shield is optically clear with anti-static coating. All seams are ultrasonically welded, no stitching. A narrow laminated panel on the left forearm accepts a BCI proximity ID card. Geneware workers with tails or wings cannot use standard Type-C — they require the gene-compatible Type-G variant at three times the cost.
functionality: Rated ISO Class 5 particulate exclusion. ESD dissipation prevents static discharge near sensitive fab equipment. Integrated BCI ID panel logs entry/exit times automatically. Positive-pressure hood option available on Type-C Plus variant. Single-use or up to 12 sterilization cycles before mandatory disposal.
what_it_says: You work somewhere clean enough that your body is considered a contamination risk.
manufacturer: Nullvault Sterile Systems (Corponation subsidiary of Helix Corp)
price_range: Φ 45–Φ 120 per unit (bulk facility purchase Φ 28/unit)
story_hooks: A geneware clinic has been cutting costs by reusing single-use Type-C suits past the 12-cycle limit — and a contamination outbreak is being quietly suppressed.
A chip fab worker has been smuggling data out encoded in the BCI ID log metadata — no one has noticed because the logs are auto-archived and never reviewed.
A Type-C suit was found abandoned in a Tier 1 drainage channel, still sealed, with biological material inside that doesn't match any known geneware profile.

physical_description.visual_profile: A pristine, ghost-white full-body coverall that reads clinical and sterile. The garment envelops the wearer completely—sealed hood with integrated clear face shield, booties fused to leg openings, triple-layered glove cuffs extending past wrists. The silhouette is boxy and featureless, emphasizing function over form. It has the austere, antiseptic appearance of medical or pharmaceutical-grade PPE.
physical_description.fit: Loose, intentionally oversized to accommodate layering underneath and allow unrestricted movement in laboratory environments. The coverall hangs straight from shoulders to ankles with no tapering. Glove cuffs are deliberately voluminous to overlap protective sleeves worn beneath.
physical_description.primary_material: Electrostatically dissipative polyethylene composite—a synthetic blend engineered for contamination control and static suppression. Shell has a waxy, rigid texture characteristic of industrial-grade cleanroom polymers.
physical_description.texture: Stiff and plastic-like with an audible crinkle at every movement. The surface is smooth but slightly tacky from the anti-static coating. Seams are ultrasonically welded, creating subtle raised ridges where panels bond. The material has a faint antiseptic, chemical odor embedded in the polymer itself that persists through multiple washes.
physical_description.color_scheme: Bright white with a faint pearl sheen from the dissipative coating. All hardware and closures are polished chrome or stainless steel. The laminated ID card panel on the left forearm is metallic silver with a holographic verification stripe.
physical_description.closures: No visible zippers or mechanical closures—the entire suit is sealed via ultrasonication. Access is gained by carefully peeling seams apart at designated break points. The face shield hinges open on micro-magnetic latches. The ID card panel uses friction-fit retention.
distinctive_features: Ultrasonically welded seams throughout—no stitching visible
Integrated sealed hood with optically clear anti-static face shield
Triple-layer glove cuffs designed for overlap with secondary gloves
Fused booties with reinforced sole grip pattern
Laminated BCI proximity ID card acceptance panel on left forearm
Electrostatic dissipative surface coating (visible as faint milky sheen)
Manufactured branding: 'NULLVAULT' embossed subtly on upper left chest
Engineered asymmetry—all functional panels positioned for right-handed access
No pockets, no hardware protrusions, no external attachment points
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 corporate. This is expensive, purpose-built cleanroom equipment. Only accessible to chip fabrication technicians, geneware clinic staff, and other high-tier pharmaceutical/biotech workers. The Helix Corp subsidiary pricing ensures gatekeeping.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this signals employment in sterile, high-value industries—geneware modification clinics, advanced chip fabs, genetic research. It's a badge of corporate legitimacy and technical expertise. In sub-grade zones, a worn Nullvault suit is either a priceless salvage item or signals black-market biotech work.
physical_description.condition_typical: New suits are pristine and crinkly. After 50+ hours of use, creases develop in the hood and at joints from repeated sealing/unsealing. The white develops a grayish patina from residual antiseptic vapor and handling. The face shield may develop micro-scratches. Well-maintained suits show no tears; damaged seams render the suit unusable for Class-10 work and are typically discarded or sold to salvage networks.
